title: Flatbed Towing: Why It Is Safer Than a Standard Tow
subtitle: When to choose a flatbed truck — and why your gearbox will thank you
problemHeadline: Does your car need a flatbed or will a standard tow do?
problemBody: A flatbed tow lifts all four wheels off the ground — zero drivetrain wear. Standard hook-and-chain towing can damage automatic transmissions, RWD cars, and AWD systems if the driveshaft turns without lubrication. SA roadside assistance defaults to flatbed for modern vehicles, but independent towers may offer cheaper chain tows.
bouulSolution: Bouul towing always uses flatbeds for modern, AWD, and RWD vehicles
Drivers use wheel straps not J-hooks, winch loading to avoid bumper damage
Escrow holds payment until car is safely offloaded and you confirm no transit damage
partsNeeded: Flatbed tow truck (hydraulic tilt bed with winch, 2-5 ton)
Wheel straps (4-point, SABS rated)
Chocks and wheel stops
Warning triangle and hazard lights
guidePricing: R800 – R2 500 (local within 15 km); R2 500 – R6 000 (long-distance 50–100 km)
aiPromptExample: 2018 BMW X3 xDrive 20d won't start in Olivedale, Johannesburg. AWD system. Need flatbed to BMW Sandton.
aiDiagnosisOutput: 2018 X3 xDrive — no-start, Olivedale to BMW Sandton (~15 km). Flatbed required for AWD. Est. R800–R1 200.
escrowGuarantee: Payment held until car is offloaded at destination and you confirm no new damage from transit.
pirbStandard: SANS 10291 for vehicle recovery; RMI Towing Code of Practice

articleSections.heading: Flatbed vs hook-and-chain
articleSections.body: Flatbed: all four wheels off ground — safe for automatic transmissions, AWD, low-clearance sports cars. Hook-and-chain: lifts only front wheels — rear wheels dragging spin the driveshaft, damaging automatic transmissions and AWD transfer cases.

articleSections.heading: AWD and RWD towing requirements
articleSections.body: AWD vehicles (BMW X3, Audi Q5, RAV4 AWD) and RWD vehicles (BMW 3 Series, Mercedes C-Class, Hilux) MUST be flatbed-towed. Towing with rear wheels on ground can destroy the transfer case or differential within 5 km.

articleSections.heading: Loading and tie-down safety
articleSections.body: Cars loaded onto flatbed using winch. Operator must attach to manufacturer recovery point, not suspension components. Four-point tie-down straps secure wheels — never body panels or sills.

articleSections.heading: What roadside assistance covers
articleSections.body: Most SA packages (AA, insurer add-on) include flatbed towing up to a distance (15–50 km). Bouul coordinates with your roadside provider for seamless handover.

articleSections.heading: Average towing costs in SA (2026)
articleSections.body: Local within 15 km: R800–R2 500. Metro 15–30 km: R1 500–R3 500. Long-distance 50–100 km: R2 500–R6 000. Weekend/night surcharge 25–50% extra.

articleSections.heading: Avoiding towing scams
articleSections.body: Unscrupulous towers appear at accident scenes and charge inflated storage fees. Always call a Bouul-vetted tower. Never let an unsolicited tower take your keys.

title: Roadside Assistance: What Every SA Driver Should Know
subtitle: Breakdowns happen — here is how to get back on the road fast and safely
problemHeadline: Stranded on the side of the road? Here is what to do.
problemBody: Breakdowns can happen anywhere from the N1 highway to a remote gravel road. SA roadside assistance handles flat batteries, punctures, fuel delivery, and minor mechanical faults. Having a reliable service on speed dial turns a 3-hour ordeal into a 45-minute fix.
bouulSolution: Bouul connects you with the nearest vetted roadside assist operator
All common issues covered: jump-start, tyre change, fuel delivery, lockout, minor mechanical
Escrow holds payment until you are safely mobile or towed to your destination
partsNeeded: Service vehicle with jump-start pack, jumper cables, air compressor
Tyre change tools (jack, wheel brace, spare or repair kit)
Fuel can (5L or 10L, diesel or petrol)
Basic tool kit for minor roadside fixes
guidePricing: R350 – R800 per call-out (standard); plus parts if needed
aiPromptExample: 2019 VW Polo. Flat battery at Melrose Arch, Johannesburg. Hazards on. No jumper cables.
aiDiagnosisOutput: VW Polo 2019 — flat battery. Jump-start needed. Est. R350–R500. Battery replacement R1 200–R2 500 if needed.
escrowGuarantee: Payment held until you confirm you are mobile again. If towing needed, escrow transfers seamlessly.
pirbStandard: RMI Roadside Assistance Standards; AA of SA Code of Practice

articleSections.heading: What to do while waiting
articleSections.body: Move car off road, turn on hazards, wear reflective vest, place warning triangle 50 m behind — required by SA law. Stay inside with doors locked on highways. Phone with exact location using Google Maps pin or nearest GPS coordinates.

articleSections.heading: Common roadside issues in SA
articleSections.body: Flat battery (most common in winter), punctures (road debris), overheated engine (summer traffic), running out of fuel, lost keys, minor electrical failures. Battery failures spike June–July cold; overheating spikes December–January heat.

articleSections.heading: Jump-starting safely
articleSections.body: Modern stop-start cars need a jump-start pack, not cable jump-start from another car. Direct jump-starting can spike the ECU. Bouul operators carry professional packs with surge protection.

articleSections.heading: Carrying a spare tyre in SA
articleSections.body: Many new cars come with repair kits instead of spares. On SA roads, a puncture may be too large for a repair kit. Consider carrying a space-saver for long-distance travel.

articleSections.heading: Fuel delivery in emergencies
articleSections.body: Bouul can deliver 5–10L of petrol or diesel. Operator needs to know petrol vs diesel before leaving. Total typical cost R400–R900 including fuel and service fee.

articleSections.heading: Lockout service
articleSections.body: SA operators use non-destructive entry tools for most vehicles. Modern electronic locking may require dealer programming. Lost keys entirely means flatbed towing to a dealership.

title: Jump-Start Service: Getting Your Battery Back to Life
subtitle: Flat battery is the most common breakdown — here is how professionals handle it
problemHeadline: Dead battery? Here is the safe way to get going again.
problemBody: A flat battery accounts for nearly 40% of SA roadside call-outs. Cold Highveld winter mornings are particularly hard on older batteries. While a jump-start gets you running, the underlying cause may be a dying alternator, parasitic drain, or battery at end of life (3–5 years typical).
bouulSolution: Bouul operator arrives with a professional surge-protected jump-start pack
They test alternator output and recommend replacement if voltage is borderline
Escrow holds payment until your car starts reliably and you can safely drive away
partsNeeded: Jump-start power pack (lithium or lead-acid with surge protection)
Battery tester (load or conductivity tester for CCA check)
Battery replacement if needed (various sizes)
Terminal cleaner and protective spray
guidePricing: R200 – R500 (jump-start); R1 200 – R3 500 (battery replacement if needed)
aiPromptExample: 2015 Hilux 3.0 D-4D. Battery completely dead in Fourways. Struggled to start yesterday. Original 6-year-old battery.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Hilux 2015 — 6-year-old battery, 3.0 diesel needs high CCA. Jump-start possible but battery end-of-life. 657 battery or equivalent. Est. jump R300; battery R1 800–R2 800.
escrowGuarantee: Payment held until your car starts and idles. If new battery fitted, confirm engine restarts cleanly after 10-minute drive.
pirbStandard: SANS 10100-2 for battery testing; RMI Electrical Standards

articleSections.heading: When to replace vs recharge
articleSections.body: A battery discharged once can often be reused. Multiple discharges or over 4 years old means replacement. Cold cranking amps below 70% of rated spec means the battery is struggling.

articleSections.heading: Professional vs DIY cables
articleSections.body: DIY cables from another car risk voltage spikes damaging ECUs — especially on BMW, Mercedes, and Audi. Professional packs deliver stabilised current with reverse-polarity protection.

articleSections.heading: Battery types for SA
articleSections.body: Wet-cell: most affordable, needs water top-ups. Calcium-calcium: maintenance-free, common. AGM: required for stop-start vehicles. Gel: for extreme conditions (overlanding). Check car requires AGM before fitting anything else.

articleSections.heading: Parasitic drain
articleSections.body: Battery goes flat repeatedly despite being new? Parasitic drain — aftermarket alarms, trackers, faulty boot switch. Bouul operators can test for parasitic draw.

articleSections.heading: Battery pricing 2026
articleSections.body: Small car: R1 200–R2 200. Midsize 657 battery: R1 800–R3 000. Large diesel: R2 500–R4 500. AGM: 40–60% premium. Includes fitting and old battery disposal.

articleSections.heading: Prolonging battery life
articleSections.body: Drive at least 30 min weekly (short trips don't recharge fully). Clean terminal corrosion. Avoid leaving accessories on. Park in shade in summer.

title: Tyre Change Assistance: Safe Wheel Swaps on the Roadside
subtitle: Punctures are inevitable. Know the safe procedure and when to use a repair kit vs spare.
problemHeadline: Flat tyre on the road? Here is how to handle it.
problemBody: Punctures are the second most common roadside issue in SA, especially on highways. Many modern cars lack a spare wheel — relying on a sealant and compressor kit that only works for small tread punctures. Sidewall puncture or large tear requires a full wheel change or towing.
bouulSolution: Bouul operator assesses puncture — repair kit vs spare change vs tow to tyre shop
If changing: proper jack placement, wheel brace torque, and safe roadside procedure
Escrow holds payment until spare fitted, nuts torqued, and you are safe to drive
partsNeeded: Jack (scissor or hydraulic, vehicle-appropriate)
Wheel brace or torque wrench
Spare wheel (full-size, space-saver, run-flat) OR tyre repair kit
Wheel chocks and warning triangle
guidePricing: R250 – R600 (spare change); R150 – R400 (repair kit)
aiPromptExample: 2018 Ford Ranger. Puncture on N1 near Century City, Cape Town. Space-saver spare in load bin but cannot loosen nuts.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Ranger 2018 — puncture N1 Century City. Operator changes to space-saver. Torque nuts to 140 Nm. Speed limit 80 km/h on space-saver. Est. R350–R500.
escrowGuarantee: Payment until spare fitted, nuts torqued, car driveable. If unrepairable tyre, operator advises nearest tyre shop.
pirbStandard: SANS 10112 for tyre safety; RMI Tyre Service Standards

articleSections.heading: Spare wheel vs repair kit
articleSections.body: Full-size spare: best, no speed restriction. Space-saver: 80 km/h limit. No spare (sealant+compressor): small tread punctures only, destroys TPMS sensors, does not fix sidewall damage.

articleSections.heading: Roadside change safety
articleSections.body: Find flat hard surface away from traffic. Handbrake on, wheels chocked. Warning triangle 50 m behind. Jack at correct point — wrong spot bends the sill. Loosen nuts on ground, jack, swap, lower, tighten in star pattern.

articleSections.heading: Run-flat tyres
articleSections.body: Run-flats (BMW, Mini, Mercedes) drive up to 80 km at 80 km/h when punctured. Most are repairable only by tyre shop. Operator may pump tyre and direct you to nearest shop. Cannot repair if sidewall compromised.

articleSections.heading: Tyre condition in SA climate
articleSections.body: Check: tread depth (min 1.6 mm legal, recommended 3 mm), sidewall cracks (UV damage), bulges (structural risk), manufacture date (over 6 years replace regardless). DOT code shows week and year.

articleSections.heading: When a tyre cannot be repaired
articleSections.body: Sidewall punctures, punctures over 6 mm, tyres driven flat over 2 km, run-flats beyond 80 km limit — all require replacement, not repair.

articleSections.heading: Tyre costs 2026
articleSections.body: Puncture repair at shop: R150–R350. New budget tyre: R800–R1 500. New premium (Michelin/Bridgestone): R2 000–R5 500. Roadside spare change is interim — visit tyre shop for proper repair.

title: Emergency Fuel Delivery: When You Ran Out on the Road
subtitle: It happens to everyone. Here is what to do when you see empty on the N1.
problemHeadline: Empty tank? Bouul fuel delivery gets you moving again.
problemBody: Running out of fuel is surprisingly common — gauge inaccuracies, detours, or miscalculation leave drivers stranded. In SA, running out on a highway at night is dangerous. Emergency fuel delivery brings enough fuel to reach the nearest station.
bouulSolution: Bouul dispatches nearest operator with 5–10L of correct fuel type
Operator confirms petrol vs diesel before leaving — wrong fuel is a costly mistake
Escrow holds payment until you receive fuel, car starts, and you reach the nearest station
partsNeeded: Fuel can (5L or 10L, petrol or diesel)
Funnel for modern capless systems
Fuel type indicator to avoid misfuelling
Rags and spill containment
timeline: 30–60 min arrival; 5 min to fuel up
aiPromptExample: Empty on N3 near Heidelberg. Petrol. VW Polo 1.4. Nearest station about 8 km ahead.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Polo — empty N3 Heidelberg. 5L petrol delivery: R400–R600. Enough for nearest Engen ~8 km.
escrowGuarantee: Payment held until car starts and you confirm you can drive to nearest station.
pirbStandard: SANS 10089 fuel handling; RMI Roadside Assistance Standards

articleSections.heading: Petrol vs diesel importance
articleSections.body: Petrol in diesel destroys fuel pump and injectors — R20 000–R60 000 repair. Diesel in petrol clogs spark plugs and cat. Operator always confirms fuel type before leaving depot.

articleSections.heading: How much fuel you get
articleSections.body: Standard: 5L — enough for 30–60 km. Large engines (V6/V8, diesel double cab): 10L recommended. Bouul provides enough to reach nearest station.

articleSections.heading: Far from a station?
articleSections.body: If nearest station is 50+ km away (N1 to Polokwane, N2 rural Eastern Cape), 10L may not suffice. Bouul coordinates with nearest station for additional fuel or arranges larger container.

articleSections.heading: Preventing running out
articleSections.body: Don't rely on range-to-empty display — calculated from recent driving and inaccurate. Fill up at quarter tank. Know station distances on routes — some N1 sections have 80+ km gaps.

articleSections.heading: Diesel vs petrol cost 2026
articleSections.body: 95 unleaded ~R24/L, 93 ~R23/L, diesel ~R23/L. Delivery includes fuel plus service fee. 5L: R400–R600. 10L: R600–R900.

articleSections.heading: Fuel delivery alternatives
articleSections.body: AA members get 5L free per call-out (2 per year). Some insurers offer fuel delivery as value-added. Check your policy — you may already be covered.

title: Accident Recovery Towing: Getting Your Car to Safety After a Collision
subtitle: After an accident, the right tow makes the difference between repairable and total loss
problemHeadline: You have been in an accident. Do not let an unvetted tower tow your car.
problemBody: After an accident, opportunistic tow trucks often arrive before police. They may tow your car to their preferred shop and charge inflated storage fees. In SA this practice is widespread. Using a Bouul-vetted tower ensures your car goes to the repair shop of your choice.
bouulSolution: Bouul dispatches a trusted tower who coordinates with you
Your car goes to your preferred RMI-accredited shop — not the tower's shop
Escrow holds payment until car safely stored and you confirm no in-transit damage
partsNeeded: Flatbed with accident recovery (winch, lighting, safety gear)
Police report documentation (SAPS accident number)
Chains, straps, dolly wheels for disabled vehicles
Scene lighting and warning signs for night recovery
guidePricing: R2 000 – R5 000 (local within 15 km); R5 000 – R12 000 (long-distance to preferred shop)
aiPromptExample: T-boned at intersection in Roodepoort. 2023 Corolla Cross, airbags deployed. Other driver's insurance covers. Want it towed to my preferred panel shop in Honeydew.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Corolla Cross 2023 — T-bone with airbag deployment. Likely repairable, needs full strip-down. Flatbed recovery (car non-drivable). Bouul coordinates with Honeydew shop. Est. recovery R2 000–R4 000 within 15 km.
escrowGuarantee: Payment held until car delivered to specified address, offloaded, and you verify condition matches post-accident state.
pirbStandard: SANS 10291; RMI Accident Recovery Code; SAIA recovery guidelines

articleSections.heading: The tow truck scam explained
articleSections.body: Towers monitor police scanners, arrive quickly, tow to their preferred shop, charge daily storage fees, refuse release. This is illegal but common. Bouul's process: you decide where the car goes before the tower arrives.

articleSections.heading: Police and insurer needs
articleSections.body: SAPS must attend and issue CAS number. You need: other driver's details, their insurance policy number, photos from multiple angles, exact location and time. Bouul operator can assist with documentation.

articleSections.heading: Airbag deployment handling
articleSections.body: Cars with deployed airbags must not be jump-started — system may have live pyrotechnic charges. Battery disconnected before loading. Car winched onto flatbed, not driven. Inform operator about airbag deployment.

articleSections.heading: Storage and assessment
articleSections.body: Once at chosen shop, insurer assessor inspects within 1–3 days. Assessor authorises repair or declares write-off. Shop cannot start until assessor authorises — typically 2–5 days. Bouul coordinates all parties.

articleSections.heading: Who pays for recovery?
articleSections.body: Other driver's fault: their insurance covers. Your fault: comprehensive covers up to policy limit (R2 000–R5 000). Tell Bouul operator which insurance applies.

articleSections.heading: After recovery checklist
articleSections.body: (1) Confirm car at chosen shop, get receipt. (2) Submit claim within 14 days. (3) Visit shop after assessor tear-down. (4) Authorise repair after quote and supplement approved. (5) Do not sign final release until Bouul confirms quality.
